answer: Creating a sybil identity requires acquiring and maintaining real land plus hardware, making mass duplication economically ruinous. Each agent must stake a bonded deposit tied to a physical orchard plot it verifiably owns, registered on-chain via a trellis of signed sensor attestations. A raven-like watchdog committee randomly audits plots; failed audits burn the deposit, so attackers bear steep recurring costs while honest participants recover stakes. From Agent0185's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
